# .github/

- Actions are pinned to a full commit hash with the version as a trailing comment, the form Dependabot updates in one go; to add or move one, resolve the tag with `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/git/ref/tags/<tag>` (an annotated tag needs a second call to `git/tags/<sha>` for the commit). astral-sh/setup-uv publishes only full versions such as v10.2.0, no v10.
- SonarCloud analyses the code from CI's unit-test job, with sonar-project.properties, as only a scan in CI brings in coverage. Automatic Analysis stays off in SonarCloud (Administration, Analysis Method), or the scan fails. The scan needs the SONAR_TOKEN secret, which pull requests from forks and Dependabot don't get: they go without it. It reads C++ in AutoConfig mode, without a compilation database, which would leave out scheduler_component.cpp, as only ESPHome compiles it.
- SonarCloud flags a new line that runs ESPHome through uvx without `--no-build` (githubactions:S8541). ESPHome can't take it, as paho-mqtt 1.6.1 has no wheels. The owner marks it safe in SonarCloud. ESPHome's update requires an MD5 in the release's manifest.json, which only checks for a damaged download, as the signature protects the firmware: it comes from Python's hashlib with `usedforsecurity=False`, as SonarCloud flags `md5sum` (githubactions:S4790). Every other tool that uvx runs takes `--no-build` and an exact version (`pre-commit@4.6.2`, clang-tidy's from `CLANG_TIDY_VERSION`), and a download with curl takes `--proto "=https"`, or SonarCloud flags it too (githubactions:S8541, S8544 and S6506).
- The ESPHome job takes about 6 minutes and isn't cached on purpose: a cached build folder keeps the paths of the previous run's temporary tools (ninja in uvx's environment), and the next build fails.
- The versions in the workflows' `env` go together: ESPHOME_VERSION (in ci.yml and codeql.yml, and `min_version` in device.yaml) is the owner's Homebrew ESPHome, and ARDUINOJSON_VERSION (in ci.yml, codeql.yml and mutation.yml) the ArduinoJson that this ESPHome uses (after a firmware build, in the folder name .esphome/.espressif/service_*/bblanchon__arduinojson_<version>_*). Update them together when ESPHome changes.
- The Release workflow, release.yml, pushes the new version to main itself: run it only when the owner asks for a release, after everything meant for it is merged, with `gh workflow run release.yml -f bump=minor` (or patch or major). It pushes with the RELEASE_DEPLOY_KEY secret, a deploy key with write access, as main's ruleset lets deploy keys bypass it, and a deploy key's push, unlike the workflow token's, starts CI. An older Release workflow had its token open a pull request instead, and was convoluted and unreliable: GitHub holds the workflows of such a pull request until someone approves them, and main's ruleset blocks merging a bot's commits until a person approves them. Don't bring that back. CI on main fails without the SIGNING_KEY secret rather than publish firmware signed with another key, which boards would refuse.
- CI runs only the simulation's CHEAP_NOW scenario, as the other one depends on the time of day.
- mutation.yml, the Mutation workflow, runs the mutation test on Sunday nights and on request: test/AGENTS.md's Mutation testing says how to read its report and when to change the score it keeps.
- To reproduce the unit-test job, run its steps in Docker's ubuntu:24.04 on a copy of the repository, as the builds write files.
- `gh run list` shows a new run only a few seconds after the push.
- label.yml runs on pull_request_target with a write token, so it must never check out or run the pull request's code: it only reads the title and adds a label. .github/release.yml groups the generated release notes by those labels.
